suite_notes: Offline replay fixtures for the twelve in_chat_path_gate analytics-gate questions (#1682). Each fixture drives the real Spring AI ChatClient/ToolCallingAdvisor loop (OfflineReplayEvaluator, reusing SpringAiPosAssistant.buildToolCallingChatClient) against a live model, with tool execution replaced by the fixture's canned tool_responses so no backend service or database is touched. system_prompt is a representative synthetic prompt, not a byte-identical capture of a live-assembled prompt; prompt-assembly fidelity is out of scope here (see analytics-gate/README.md non-goals). tool_responses use clean, designed-only synthetic data (the EXPECTED.md 'absolute'/'seed contribution' figures), not alpha's live co-tenant-polluted numbers, so a fixture's expected values are self-consistent regardless of alpha's current data. argument key checks (arguments_contains) assert presence only, not value equality, since not every @Tool method's exact parameter surface is re-verified here (facade-contract.yaml plus each controller's real @RequestParam names were checked once for real values (startDate/endDate/asOfDate/period/etc.), and unverifiable/uncertain surfaces are left unchecked rather than guessed). Run: ./mvnw -pl pos-mcp-server -Dmcp.eval.replay=true -Dit.test=OfflineReplayEvalIT verify

fixtures.utterance: Who were our top technicians by labor revenue last month, and what was their average billed hours per completed work order?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. Call the analytics tools you are offered to compute the answer, then summarize.

offered_tools.name: getTechnicianLaborAnalytics
offered_tools.description: Returns per-technician completed work order count, billed hours and labor revenue for a date range.

offered_tools.name: getRevenueByCustomer
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer revenue for a period (decoy: not a per-technician report).

fixtures.notes: Top by labor revenue is Nadia Torres (1500.00); Alex Kim has more completed work orders but less revenue and must not be named as top.

fixtures.utterance: Which technicians had the most work orders reopened within seven days of completion this quarter?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. Call the analytics tools you are offered to compute the answer, then summarize.

offered_tools.name: workorder_getReopenedWorkorderAnalytics
offered_tools.description: Returns per-technician reopened-work-order counts within a reopen window for a date range.

fixtures.utterance: What was the average time from work order creation to invoice, by month, for the last six months?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. This question needs one getInvoicingLag call per month in the window; do not summarize a partial set of months as if it were the full answer.

offered_tools.name: getInvoicingLag
offered_tools.description: Returns the average work-order-creation-to-invoice lag in days for one date range.

fixtures.notes: Pins the #1676 declined-composition failure mode: a below-minimum call count (fewer than 6 getInvoicingLag calls) is the defect this fixture is built to catch, matching QUESTIONS.json q04.expected_plan.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers are more than 60 days past due, and what open work orders do we currently have for them?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. This question needs one aged-receivables call, then one searchWorkorders call per past-due customer; do not stop after the first call.

offered_tools.name: getAgedReceivables
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer A/R aging buckets as of a date.

offered_tools.name: searchWorkorders
offered_tools.description: Searches work orders by a query string (e.g. customer id and status).

fixtures.notes: C3 is not past due and its open work order must not appear in the answer; a composition that stops after one searchWorkorders call is the #1676 declined-composition failure this fixture pins.

fixtures.utterance: Who were our top customers by revenue over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before that?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. This comparison needs one getRevenueByCustomer call per period.

offered_tools.name: getRevenueByCustomer
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer revenue for a period.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers have not bought anything in the last 90 days but spent more than $10,000 with us in the prior year?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures.

offered_tools.name: getRevenueByCustomer
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer revenue for a period, usable to find prior-year high-value customers.

fixtures.notes: C1 spent more in the prior year but bought recently (5 days ago), so it must not appear as lapsed; C4 is the only qualifying customer.

fixtures.utterance: For our top 20 customers by revenue in the last twelve months, show revenue, invoice count, average invoice value, outstanding balance and average days to pay.
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. This needs one getRevenueByCustomer call for the ranking plus one getAgedReceivables call for outstanding balances.

offered_tools.name: getRevenueByCustomer
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer revenue, invoice count and average invoice value for a period.

offered_tools.name: getAgedReceivables
offered_tools.description: Returns per-customer outstanding balance and average days to pay as of a date.

fixtures.notes: Pins QUESTIONS.json q09.expected_plan (getRevenueByCustomer x1 + getAgedReceivables x1, #1671).

fixtures.utterance: Of the invoices we issued in the last six months, how many were paid within 30 days, 31 to 60 days, 61 to 90 days, or are still unpaid?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures. 'in the last six months' is a whole-calendar-months window, not a rolling day count.

offered_tools.name: accounting_getPaymentLagCohorts
offered_tools.description: Returns payment-lag cohort counts and amounts for invoices issued in a date window.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers make up most of our accounts receivable balance, and how much of each is past due?
fixtures.system_prompt: You are the Durion Positivity shop assistant. Answer using only tool results; never fabricate figures.

offered_tools.name: getAgedReceivables

fixtures.notes: Canned data is the six-customer designed book only (9500.00 total), not alpha's live co-tenant-polluted book; the 80% cumulative cutoff on this clean set falls at C1+C2+C3 (81.05%).

fixtures.utterance: Who were our largest vendors by spend over the last six months compared with the same six months last year?

fixtures.utterance: Which vendors have increased their average bill amount by more than 10% year over year?
